title: Development of the decisional balance scale for health behaviors after transarterial chemoembolization in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma: A Modified Delphi Study
content:
by Yujun Jiang, Wenxi Guo, Wang Feng, Xiaolin Wang

Objective

Based on the decisional balance construct within the Transtheoretical Model, a preliminary instrument for evaluating health behavior decision-making among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma following transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) was developed. The Delphi expert consultation method was then used to assess item appropriateness, the degree of expert consensus, and content validity. This process provides an empirical foundation for subsequent refinement of the scale and its further psychometric validation in clinical practice.

Method

A modified Delphi method was employed. Between 10/12/2025 and 27/01/2026, 24 experts specializing in liver cancer patient care, interventional nursing, and psychological nursing from 16 provinces (autonomous regions and municipalities) across China were invited to rate the importance and feasibility of each item.

Results

The response rates for both rounds of expert consultation were 100%. The expert authority coefficients (Cr) were 0.92 and 0.94 for rounds 1 and 2, respectively. Kendall’s coefficients of concordance (W) for importance ratings were 0.363 and 0.385, respectively; for feasibility ratings, they were 0.253 and 0.358, respectively. All differences were statistically significant (p < 0.05). The preliminary version of the final scale comprises two dimensions, namely, perceived benefits (pros) and perceived barriers (cons), covering physical activity, medication adherence, nutritional management, and follow-up care.

Conclusion

This study developed a preliminary health behavior decisional balance scale for patients with hepatocellular carcinoma following TACE. Through Delphi expert consultation, a consensus was achieved, and acceptable content validity was established. The scale provides a preliminary tool for assessing patients’ health behavior decision-making tendencies and for identifying perceived benefits and barriers to adoption of behavior. Further psychometric evaluation in clinical samples is needed to verify the reliability and validity of the scale, as well as its potential for clinical application.
